# Why we leave the leaves

Every autumn somebody asks why the fallen leaves along the hedge are not swept up, and every autumn the answer is the same: they are doing a job. A layer of leaves keeps the frost off the soil, feeds the worms that drag it down into the beds, and gives the hedgehogs somewhere to spend the winter.

By March most of it is gone, pulled under or broken down, and what is left goes on the compost heap. The beds that were covered come out of the winter darker and looser than the ones that were raked bare, and the difference shows in the first sowings, which come up faster and stronger.

So the rake stays in the shed until spring. If you want to help, leave a corner of your own plot untidy too, and see what moves in.
